ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Sick Visit — John F. Kennedy — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for influenza with stress dosing of hydrocortisone

text.paragraph: Fever, aches and cough since yesterday. [S]

Mr. Kennedy called this morning and was seen the same day. Yesterday afternoon he developed chills, aching muscles, a sore throat and a dry cough, and last night his temperature at home was 38.9 °C. Following his written sick-day rules, he doubled his hydrocortisone this morning, taking 20 mg on waking, and has 10 mg ready for noon and 10 mg for 4 pm. He has drunk plenty, with salty broth. He has not vomited or had diarrhea and has kept every tablet down. He feels weak and tired but has had no lightheadedness on standing, fainting, confusion, or abdominal pain. Several colleagues have had influenza this week. He had this season's influenza vaccine at his first visit five weeks ago. He has his emergency injection kit with him. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1948-02-16; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Flushed and tired but alert; temperature 38.6 °C, pulse 96, respirations 18, oxygen saturation 97% on room air
112/70 lying and 108/68 after three minutes standing, pulse 96 rising to 102; no postural drop
Pharynx red without exudate; tympanic membranes normal
Clear to auscultation; no crackles or wheeze

Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease), diagnosed about three months ago during an adrenal crisis while traveling abroad, on hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented 1869 diagnosis
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented diagnosis.

Chronic low back pain persisting after lumbar disc surgery; began after a football injury in college and worsened during wartime naval service; uses a corset brace; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented back history
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented back pain and operation.

Influenza due to other identified influenza virus with other respiratory manifestations

list.item:
Influenza A (J10.1). Rapid molecular test positive for influenza A. Uncomplicated influenza within 48 hours of onset in a person whose adrenal insufficiency puts him at higher risk of complications, so antiviral treatment is advised. Lungs clear and saturation normal; no sign of pneumonia. [S]
Oseltamivir 75 mg twice daily for five days.
Rest, fluids, and acetaminophen for fever and aches.
Return or call for breathlessness, chest pain, or fever lasting more than three days.

Primary adrenal insufficiency, stress dosing during a febrile illness (E27.1). He applied the sick-day rules correctly. With a fever below 39 °C, doubling the hydrocortisone is right; above 39 °C he would triple it. No sign of adrenal crisis: blood pressure steady without a postural drop, no vomiting, no confusion, sodium 135 and potassium 4.6 mmol/L, glucose 96 mg/dL. Fludrocortisone does not need to change. [S]
Hydrocortisone 20 mg on waking, 10 mg at noon and 10 mg at 4 pm while he has a fever, and for one day after it settles, then back to 10, 5 and 5 mg.
Triple the doses if his temperature goes above 39 °C.
If he vomits, cannot keep tablets down, or feels faint or confused: inject 100 mg hydrocortisone into the thigh and call 911.
Salty fluids; continue fludrocortisone 0.1 mg.
Nurse phone check tomorrow and the day after.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Diagnosis and Treatment of Primary Adrenal Insufficiency: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline (2016); Influenza Antiviral Medications: Summary for Clinicians (2026)

Follow-up: Nurse phone check tomorrow and the day after. Six-week review as planned. Call at once or use the injection and call 911 for vomiting, fainting, confusion, or severe abdominal pain. Next scheduled visit 1948-03-09: six-week review after the dose changes: electrolytes, renin, repeat thyroid tests, and back pain. [S]
